Shared World missions Water Drip Standard is a procedural-runtime-effect added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “missions runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World missions Water Drip Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World missions Water Drip Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

assets.description:
Shared World optics Angelfish Standard is a dedicated-organic-rigging added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “optics creature” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: continuous anatomical body, species-defining head, locomotion appendages, sensory features, mouth or feeding structure, skin, scale, shell, feather, or membrane system, root and animation hierarchy, habitat and schooling anchors. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Angelfish Standard. Materials and response layers include species surface material, eyes and sensory material, appendage material, habitat-aware variation. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Angelfish Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

It closes the “optics runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Bullet Impact Wood Compact. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Bullet Impact Wood Compact, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. assets.description:
Shared World optics Cloud Shadow Sweep Standard is a procedural-runtime-effect added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “optics runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Cloud Shadow Sweep Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Cloud Shadow Sweep Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

assets.description:
Shared World optics Food Warmer Full Standard is a state-aware-model-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “optics state-variant” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: base object relationship, state-defining geometry, state-defining material layer, animation transition socket, collision state, interaction state, damage or repair metadata, LOD and swap policy. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Food Warmer Full Standard. Materials and response layers include base structural material, state-specific material, hardware or damage layer, indicator material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Food Warmer Full Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Shared World optics Loc Fiber Roughness Expanded is a procedural-shader-profile added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “optics shader” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: base shading model, normal response, roughness response, view-angle response, lighting response, quality tiers, accessibility controls, editor preview profile. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Loc Fiber Roughness Expanded. Materials and response layers include shader parameter set, mask or lookup input, lighting integration, fallback material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Loc Fiber Roughness Expanded, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Shared World optics Neon Glass Expanded is a procedural-shader-profile added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “optics shader” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: base shading model, normal response, roughness response, view-angle response, lighting response, quality tiers, accessibility controls, editor preview profile. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Neon Glass Expanded. Materials and response layers include shader parameter set, mask or lookup input, lighting integration, fallback material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Neon Glass Expanded, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

assets.description:
Shared World optics Puddle Ripple Standard is a procedural-runtime-effect added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “optics runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World optics Puddle Ripple Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Puddle Ripple Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic. Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling. This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World optics Puddle Ripple Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract. Close the optics runtime-vfx gap with Shared World optics Puddle Ripple Standard. Preserve its full component, material, lifecycle, accessibility, performance, and state contract without primitive substitutions. This entry was intentionally added outside the town blueprint inventory because it is a hero or proof asset requiring explicit dimensions, components, materials, and rejection criteria.

productionBrief.placement: Place it on a named ground, wall, ceiling, counter, shelf, dock, room, vehicle, terrain, water, or gameplay socket appropriate to its use. Every foot, base, root, bracket, anchor, contact edge, and suspension point must sit flush or visibly explain how it is supported.
productionBrief.silhouetteAndProportion: The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.
productionBrief.structuralConstruction: Model the load-bearing body, panels, seams, hinges, fasteners, supports, handles, vents, feet, brackets, openings, service access, and functional hardware appropriate to the object.

materialPlan.metalRule: Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material.
materialPlan.glassRule: Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane.
materialPlan.masonryRule: Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling.
materialPlan.woodRule: Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use.
materialPlan.flexibleRule: Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling.
materialPlan.emissiveRule: Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure.

townArtDirection.style: cohesive family-friendly open-world realism matching the owning town and gameplay role

productionBrief.conditionAndWear: Apply restrained lived-in wear at contact points, lower edges, hinges, handles, feet, fasteners, drainage paths, service openings, tires, exposed corners, or frequently cleaned surfaces. Match the district’s maintenance level rather than using uniform dirt or uniform perfection.

interactionAndAnimation.guidance: Separate parts that may open, rotate, light, display, receive an item, emit particles, take damage, change material, or connect to another system.
hooks: transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it

productionBrief.collision: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision.
productionBrief.orientationAndPivot: Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center.
productionBrief.optimization: Preserve silhouette and interaction points, sharing repeated hardware and moving only microdetail into materials at lower LODs.

lod.lod0: Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 23,400 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it.
lod.lod1: Medium-range output should target roughly 10,800 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights.
lod.lod2: Far output should target roughly 3,600 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature.
lod.neverCollapse: The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.
